evidence.note: First actions: downloaded all three vendored libs from exact upstream URLs into flat /app/static/ path and immediately ran sha256sum to verify — front-loading the highest-fatality, cheapest gate before any app code.
Re-verified vendored file hashes 'still match (safe check)' and checked for forbidden files, guarding the hash/anti-cheat gate against regression mid-build.
Repeatedly inspected CSP header confirming script-src 'self' with no unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval, plus HttpOnly+SameSite cookies — verifying the strict-CSP kill-switch.
Explicitly tallied seed minimums against required thresholds (accounts≥8, statuses≥20, hashtags≥3, CW≥2, media≥2, remote accounts) rather than assuming them.
Brand palette only asserted as 'Mastodon purple' when writing styles.css; never measured against the ±5% purple range. Button label and offline-runtime serving likewise never concretely checked.

reasoning: The agent clearly triaged the fatal gates by fatality: it front-loaded the vendored-library hash/path/version gate as its very first action, verified hashes immediately and re-verified them later, checked strict CSP multiple times, tallied seed minimums against thresholds, and scanned for forbidden build-tool files — behavior matching the 8 anchor's 'front-load the cheap-but-fatal ones and verify.' However, it left the brand palette, compose button label, and offline runtime as assumed rather than measured, and never systematically enumerated all five anti-cheat rules with concrete proofs, keeping it short of the full-8/10 'managed risk register.' This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.
